scope: A resource gate on simulated downloads
title: What a gate bound does
description: A gate held concurrency at its declared bound in every run, and 24 queued jobs finished in 139 ms at the best bound against 1,113 ms at 1.
claim: The gate never admitted more downloads than its bound: in every recorded run the most in flight equalled the bound. The time to finish 24 queued jobs fell from 1,113 ms at a bound of 1 to 139 ms at 8, then rose again to 410 ms when all 24 ran at once, because the simulated service slows when it is crowded.

headline.label: recorded runs where the most downloads in flight equalled the gate bound
time to finish 24 jobs at a bound of 1 and at the best bound, 8
slower with all 24 jobs running at once than at the best bound

method.workload: 24 jobs are queued at once through a ForEach. Each passes a Network gate and awaits a simulated download of 40 ms. The simulated service stretches the wait once more than 6 downloads are in flight. 7 fixed gate bounds from 1 to 24, one recorded run each, after a warm-up run.
engines: EvalApp pipeline with Gate and ForEach
method.verification: Every job records its own timestamps, and the number of downloads in flight is counted inside the gated step, so the bound is checked against what actually ran.
method.statistic: One recording per bound, in milliseconds. A repeated recording varies by a few percent.

losses: A bound of 1 took 1,113 ms, 8.0 times the best bound. The gate does not choose its bound for you, and a bound set too low is the slowest result here.
A bound of 24, the whole batch at once, took 410 ms, 2.9 times the best bound. A higher bound is not faster when the thing behind the gate slows under load.
limits: The work is a simulated wait, not a real network. It shows how the gate and its queue behave, not the speed of any real service.
The best bound here is a property of the simulated service, which slows past 6 in flight. A real service has its own shape, which is what the tuner exists to find.
It measures the gate and does not compare EvalApp with another library.
